borrowed: A task identifies a repository base commit and a natural-language problem statement.
The fixture and success gate are versioned inputs analogous to the dataset's base_commit, FAIL_TO_PASS, and PASS_TO_PASS fields.
A candidate change is applied to a repository workspace and verified by executable tests.
The primary quality unit is whether the complete task instance is resolved.
Models receive the same exercise while model and thinking configuration vary.
Results retain success, token, duration, and cost measurements for comparison.
A compact implementation exercise is evaluated with its language-native test command.

deviations.difference: The setup uses a versioned synthetic C# fixture tree rather than SWE-bench's public issue/PR plus base_commit or an Aider Exercism task.
deviations.reason: The first setup must be self-contained, redistributable, fast, and representative of evaluation against a private repository.

deviations.difference: The model returns one replacement file in a single turn instead of producing a SWE-bench-style repository patch or using Aider edit formats and test-feedback retries.
deviations.reason: This setup isolates model and thinking-level differences from tool orchestration; future setups may omit responseFile to measure agentic editing.

deviations.difference: One deterministic project command covers both the repaired behavior and existing examples instead of separate SWE-bench FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS test lists.
deviations.reason: The tiny fixture has no stable named-test inventory; an exit-code gate preserves the same resolved/not-resolved semantics without pretending the subsets exist.

deviations.difference: Cases use fresh temporary workspace copies but generated code is not executed inside Aider's Docker isolation boundary.
deviations.reason: This setup evaluates a trusted checked-in fixture and command; any future setup that evaluates untrusted code must provide an external sandbox.

task.prompt: Return only the complete C# source for StringTools.cs implementing StringTools.IsPalindrome. Ignore punctuation, whitespace, and letter case. An empty or punctuation-only string is a palindrome. Do not use tools, Markdown fences, or explanations.
